Pianist and band leader Gap Mangione has enjoyed a successful career that spans the 1960 Jazz Brothers LPs with brother Chuck, to his own records on A&M and his current solo and big band CDs. He is a prolific arranger and performs constantly in Central New York as a soloist and as leader of the New Blues Band and Gap Mangione Big Band.
Gap was interviewed in Rochester, NY on January 11, 2012, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and I am off camera, in Greece, New York, right? We’re in Greece?
Yeah. I’m pleased to be speaking with Gap Mangione today. And I’ve been looking forward to it, because I love talking with working musicians.
It’s interesting because, you know, when you think of Rochester you think of Kodak and Bausch & Lomb and Mangione.

And I know you and your family have been a very familiar name in the area. I’m also curious about the, you know, in Utica, where I live, you have Mancuso and Montalbano and Caramanica. And here we have Ruggiero and Mangione. Now what is it with the Italian —
